transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (CEO), Jorge Ramos (CTO), Lina Park (VP Product), Ethan Cole (Head of Eng), Priya Singh (Head of CS), plus ~120 attendees online (all hands)

AGENDA:
1) Company metrics & highlights
2) Product updates (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
3) Reliability and incidents update
4) Hiring and org updates
5) Q&A

SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Strong quarter: ARR growth and improved unit economics; still working on supply-side bottlenecks for Dedicated capacity.
- Product team announced roadmap for Dedicated autoscaling and Private control plane improvements; early access signups open.
- Engineering reviewed last week's CI/outage and immediate mitigations; longer-term reliability plan started.
- Hiring push for infra and security; headcount requests due next week.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Patel: alright, good morning everyone, welcome to our November all hands, um we're gonna get started, thank you for joining, uh quick housekeeping, recording is on, slides will be shared after, and Jorge I'm handing it to you for the metrics overview.
[00:28] Jorge Ramos: great, thanks Maya. hey team, quick numbers — Q4 bookings are up 18% quarter-over-quarter, net retention ticked to 108, and our hosted unit cost per 1k tokens improved about 12% since last quarter. these are preliminary but overall very positive.
[00:48] Speaker 1 (murmur): woo 
[00:55] Jorge Ramos: on capacity, Dedicated demand continues to outpace supply in some regions, especially west coast and eu-central; our procurement and partner teams are working on additional GPU pools, and we are prioritizing customers with reserved commits. there's some wording in the deck about burst lanes, the burst lanes option should help short-term.
[01:20] Maya Patel: quick Q — how much of the workload is shifting to quantized variants? is that helping cost?
[01:28] Jorge Ramos: yes, we've rolled out a new quant profile that reduces memory by about 30% for the transformer backbones we ship; that directly improves packing and reduces per-token cost. that, plus smarter batching and prefix cache improvements, is the majority of the unit cost gains. some of the models still need kernel tuning so it's not uniform across the catalog.
[01:50] Lina Park: i'll add, from product side we also shipped model routing policies so you can route by latency tier or cost tier, which helps enterprise customers keep predictable tail latency. it's in beta for a subset of tenants.
[02:10] [Slide change noise]
[02:15] Ethan Cole: quick note — the CI incident last week was caused by a misapplied config change to the autoscaler; that triggered a cascade where some Dedicated pools scaled down aggressively and then couldn't scale back fast enough. immediate mitigations: rollback and hotfix, improved guardrails and alerts. long-term: a throttled control-plane rollout and better safety checks. post-mortem doc will be shared.
[02:43] Maya Patel: thank you Ethan. can you surface the timeline for the post-mortem to the leadership channel?
[02:49] Ethan Cole: yes, aiming for a doc by monday nov 8, and a follow-up eng review on tuesday.
[02:56] Priya Singh: from CS perspective, we had increased inbound from enterprise customers worried about the incident; good news is our SLA fallbacks worked, most apps didn't see degraded p95 beyond 2x baseline thanks to model fallback to hosted variants. but we should get the security FAQ and SOC2 artifacts in the customer portal asap — i'm coordinating that.
[03:20] Audience (chat): where's SOC 2 report?
[03:24] Priya Singh: i'll post the link after this call, it's being updated, it's the v2 evidence pack.
[03:31] [10s silence while slides load]
[03:45] Lina Park: product roadmap briefly — next 90 days: 1) Dedicated autoscaling 2) Private control plane improvements (SSO, KMS rotation workflows, audit log export), 3) Optimize for multi-tenant quantized kernels and 4) embeddings throughput improvements.
[04:08] Speaker 2: can you say more about KMS and rotation?
[04:12] Lina Park: yeah, short answer: Private customers will get a smoother KMS rotation path and a documented HSM pattern for BYOK; also better audit log retention options for compliance.
[04:23] Maya Patel: also cross-functional note — the product and security folks are working with some customers on air-gapped private deployments, e.g., regulated financials; expect a playbook for that next month.
[04:40] Jorge Ramos: technical deep dive highlight — we've been experimenting with kernel selection improvements for long-context workloads and dynamic kv cache eviction heuristics; initial benchmarks show a 15% latency reduction for sequences over 8k tokens. that's still research but very promising.
[05:05] Attendee (Samir, Eng): is that the same heuristic that caused the cache thrash before?
[05:09] Jorge Ramos: good call out — no, we've added extra telemetry and backpressure to avoid thrash; there's more logic to favor hot prefixes. we'll post the benchmark notebook in the tech-readme.
[05:25] [crowd laughter]
[05:30] Maya Patel: hiring update — we've got approval to open 18 roles this quarter across infra, security, and customer success. please work with your managers and talent ops to prioritize. we are intentionally hiring for senior infra engineers and a principal product security role.
[05:53] Priya Singh: CS note — rolling out a new onboarding playbook, it's shorter and has a quickstart for Dedicated customers to reduce time to first qps.
[06:05] Audience question (chat): will there be more office space in sf?
[06:09] Maya Patel: short answer: yes, we secured more desks in the mid-market building; details in the slack channel.
[06:16] [brief silence]
[06:22] Lina Park: demo time — quick look at the new console traces: here's a per-model latency heatmap and token-level cost breakdown; you can drill into a route and see token-level traces and KV cache hit ratios. the demo is a bit rough in the recording audio because of, uh, network hiccup.
[06:48] [demo audio glitch]
[07:00] Lina Park: okay moving on, integrations — we shipped a marketplace listing with two cloud partners; that should make procurement easier for customers who want private or dedicated in their cloud accounts.
[07:15] [questions queued]
[07:20] Employee (Rachel, Sales): can we get a one-pager on the pricing changes for Dedicated? customers asking about committed vs burst lanes.
[07:29] Maya Patel: yes, sales ops will publish a pricing FAQ, Lina will coordinate with finance, target date Nov 12.
[07:38] Jorge Ramos: ops update — we've improved eviction policies to favor small requests, that reduces tail latency for conversational (chat) workloads; also we added extra tracing hooks to help debug memory fragmentation issues, which should help when we tune kernels for quantized models.
[08:05] Audience (chat rapid): nice, thanks
[08:10] Ethan Cole: security — we completed our internal threat modeling for the Private control plane, and are testing audit log exports into customers' SIEMs. plus some customers asked for RBAC groups to match their orgs, that's coming next quarter.
[08:30] Employee question (DevRel): will the SDK changes be backwards compatible?
[08:34] Lina Park: yes, we're keeping the major API stable; there will be a new header for routing hints but existing calls will continue to work. we'll publish migration notes.
[08:45] [applause emoji spam in chat]
[08:50] Maya Patel: okay, open Q&A; remind people to use the mic or drop in chat.
[09:00] Employee (Alex, PM): curious about cash runway and fundraising?
[09:04] Maya Patel: team, we're in a good position; closed a strategic partnership last month that improved committed revenue visibility; runway covers 18+ months with current burn assumptions, and we are opportunistically talking to investors but no active raise right now.
[09:26] Speaker (whisper): good to hear 
[09:30] Employee (Ops): any change to holiday policy?
[09:33] Maya Patel: no changes planned; standard blackout for oncall rotations might apply for Dec 24-26 for some teams, we'll share specifics in HR.
[09:44] [crosstalk]
[09:50] Priya Singh: customer highlight — shoutout to the onboarding team for a successful POC with a fintech customer using Private; they validated latency SLOs and data residency needs. leads to expansion conversations.
[10:05] Ethan Cole: quick infra note — we've started a pilot with a new GPU partner in eu-central that gives us better spot capacity for burst lanes; still early.
[10:15] Audience (chat): will that change pricing?
[10:18] Maya Patel: no immediate change to published pricing; spot/burst economics will be reflected in newer guidance for sales.
[10:25] [short silence]
[10:30] Lina Park: product experiment highlight — we tried automatic model fallback that chooses a cheaper variant on high load; customers on the POC saw small quality diffs but large cost savings. we want to make that opt-in and provide control.
[10:50] Employee (DevRel): can we get an opt-in flag?
[10:53] Lina Park: yes, it's a per-route policy and we'll expose it in the console.
[11:00] Maya Patel: wrapping up — thanks everyone for the hard work, Q4 is a big quarter. recap of immediate next steps: post-mortem by Nov 8 (Ethan), product timeline by Nov 12 (Lina), SOC2/FAQ links by Nov 9 (Priya), headcount requests by Nov 12 (people managers).
[11:25] [applause]
[11:30] Maya Patel: recording will be uploaded; please file questions in #all-hands-questions. see you at the holiday party sign-up sheet.
[11:40] End of recording.
